record_title: The first-repeat law identifies the atomic mass spectrum
provenance: Inverse identification theorem for iid first-repeat times: an exact entire-function factorization recovers all atom masses and the total nonatomic mass, with a finite-horizon corollary under a finite atom bound.
limitations: Population-level identification rather than statistical stability; atom locations and the internal nonatomic law are invisible; the 2m+1 finite-horizon bound is sufficient rather than asserted optimal; older generalized-birthday work, especially Stein (1990), leaves residual priority uncertainty.
